meta.produced_by: EdgeTRM/mcu_h1.py (p4d, ~/venvs/mcu: torch 2.13, litert_torch 0.9.4, ai_edge_quantizer 0.9.0, ai_edge_litert 2.2.0, ethos-u-vela 5.2.0)
meta.units: sram/flash/dram *_memory_used in KiB (Vela summary CSV); inference_time in seconds as in the CSV, inference_ms = 1e3 * inference_time; *_bytes are bytes per inference; cycles are NPU cycles and exclude operators Vela leaves on the CPU (see cpu_operators)
meta.calibration: real carries from ~/aihub_artifacts/h1/<task>/calib_H<H>.npz (aihub_h1.py --stage calib); last 4 samples held out for the numerical check
meta.acceptance_vela_config: ethos-u55-256 / Ethos_U55_High_End_Embedded / Shared_Sram (the Corstone-300 FVP configuration)
notes: Maze on U55/U65: Vela's per-layer CSV for maze H=1 INT8 (U55-256, Shared_Sram) puts 82.0% of NPU cycles in the 20 attention BatchMatMuls (916 tokens). The 263 MiB off-chip flash is the compiled graph's 'read_only' buffer (275,560,752 B); the Softmax-lowering Add ops are the ones reading it (2.68e8 flash accesses), consistent with one [8,916,916] 32-bit constant (26.8 MB) per softmax x 10 softmax ops at H=1 (30 at H=3: 776 MiB). On U85-256 (SYS_Flash_High) the same H=1 graph needs 7,620 KiB (7.4 MiB) of flash.

W8A16 cycles exclude CPU fallbacks: on U55/U65 the attention BATCH_MATMULs with INT16 inputs stay on the CPU (Vela: 'IF Matmul or (FC with dynamic weights): IFM precision must be Int8'; 28 ops for sudoku_attn H=1, 20 for maze H=1), so W8A16 attention rows are not comparable with INT8 rows.

Vela version sensitivity: the eval kit's Vela 5.1.0 estimates 136.8 M / 332.5 M cycles for the same H=1 Sudoku-MLP / Sudoku-Attn INT8 graphs on U55-256 (5.2.0: 52.0 M / 162.5 M; H=3: 410.3 M / 997.1 M vs 155.8 M / 487.5 M). The FVP runs the 5.2.0-compiled stream (mcu_h1_raw/vela510_crosscheck.json).

FVP attention caveat: Vela lowers each U55 BATCH_MATMUL into ELEMENTWISE MUL (int8 x int8 -> int32) plus POOL REDUCE_SUM with an int32 IFM and int8 OFM. The FVP's Ethos-U55/U65 model (rev 136b7d75, Apr 2023) prints '[critical] Op=4: Invalid data type, ifm=5 ofm=1' once per such command (2,254 per H=1 Sudoku-Attn step on U55, the exact count in the register stream). The run completes, but its attention cycle count is not a validated measurement. The MLP-mixing graphs contain no matmul and run clean.

TFLite Micro numerics: every graph TFLM invokes returns a single repeated output value (for sudoku_mlp H=1 INT8, every logit at the output zero point). Traced on sudoku_mlp H=1 INT8 (mcu_ref_kernel_diff.py): the builtin reference kernels, which TFLM shares, get the RMS-norm INT8 REDUCE SUM wrong (exact integer result -127/-128, optimized kernel -127/-128, reference kernel and TFLM -1); earlier ops differ by at most 14 LSB. TFLM arenas are valid; a CPU-only TFLM deployment of these graphs is not numerically valid without a fix to that kernel. Maze invokes abort (SIGABRT, no message).

INT4 on Ethos-U: no TFLite route (Vela docs: 'Weight tensors must be 8-bit precision' for FULLY_CONNECTED; Vela 5.2.0 crashes with SIGFPE in regor.compile on every graph with an INT4 FULLY_CONNECTED, down to a single Linear; 5.1.0 crashes the same way on the Sep 10 W4A8 graph). The documented route is TOSA (EXT-INT4; CONV2D (i8,i4,i32)), e.g. ExecuTorch's Arm backend; the TOSA tables above show Vela 5.2 accepting INT4 weights. Evidence: mcu_h1_raw/int4/int4_notes.json.
Ethos_U55_High_End_Embedded + Dedicated_Sram is not a valid Vela configuration (arena_mem_area=OffChipFlash); it fails at every H exactly as in the Sep 10 sweep and is kept for completeness.

notes.question: Why does every W4A8 TFLite graph fail in Vela 5.2.0 (rc=-8), and is there any documented route for INT4 weights onto an Ethos-U NPU?
notes.vela_version: ethos-u-vela 5.2.0 (~/venvs/mcu); cross-checked with 5.1.0 (the eval kit's resources_downloaded/env)

findings.what: rc=-8 is signal 8 (SIGFPE). Running vela under `python -X faulthandler` gives no Vela diagnostic, only: 'Fatal Python error: Floating point exception ... File ".../ethosu/vela/vela.py", line 137 in process_regor', i.e. inside the C++ core call regor.compile(). --verbose-all prints nothing before the crash.
reproduced_on: H=3 Sep 10 w4a8 graph (mixed float/INT8, INT4 FC)
H=1 w4a8_c and w4a8_t (all-INT8 graph, INT4 FULLY_CONNECTED), all three tasks
a single Linear(512,1536) on [1,97,512] quantized W4A8 per-channel and per-tensor (mcu_int4_min.py); the same Linear at W8A8 compiles (1 NPU op, 0 CPU ops)
findings.cause: INT4 weight tensors on FULLY_CONNECTED. Not the float operators of the H=3 graph: the all-INT8 H=1 graphs whose only non-INT8 tensors are the INT4 FC weights crash the same way.

findings.what: Vela's generated SUPPORTED_OPS.md (vela --supported-ops-report, 5.2.0) lists for FULLY_CONNECTED, CONV_2D, DEPTHWISE_CONV_2D, TRANSPOSE_CONV on Ethos-U55/U65 and on Ethos-U85: 'Weight tensors must be 8-bit precision'. The expected behaviour for an INT4 FC would be CPU fallback; regor instead crashes with SIGFPE (a Vela defect).
regor_binary_strings: Weight DType not INT8 and zero point not 0

findings.what: --debug-force-legacy-core (deprecated Python core, U55/U65 TFLite only): the H=3 graph hits 'RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded' in pass_packing; with --recursion-limit 20000 the H=1 w4a8_c graph compiles but every FULLY_CONNECTED goes to the CPU ('Unsupported TensorFlow Lite semantics for FULLY_CONNECTED ... Placing on CPU instead' / 'Constant tensors should not have NoneType-values' / 'Unexpected None value for constant tensor'), NPU ops 264 (74.8%), nn_macs 1.43 M vs 4.28 G for the INT8 graph. The legacy reader also reads the W8A8 single-Linear's constant as None, so it cannot read AEQ-exported constants at all; it says nothing about INT4 support.

Vela documents INT4 weights for TOSA input only. SUPPORTED_OPS.md, 'Ethos-U55 and Ethos-U65 TOSA Generic Constraints': 'PRO-INT extensions: ... EXT-INT4: 4-bit integer weights'; 'For TOSA operators, CPU fallback is not supported.'; TOSA CONV2D / DEPTHWISE / TRANSPOSE_CONV2D 'DataTypes (IFM, Weights, OFM): (i8_t,i8_t,i32_t), (i8_t,i4_t,i32_t), (i16_t,i8_t,i48_t)'. Ethos-U85 TOSA: 'Supported extensions: EXT-INT16, EXT-INT4, EXT-DOUBLEROUND'.
findings.test: mcu_tosa_int4.py: a hand-serialized TOSA 1.0 graph (tosa-tools 2026.2.1) with the TRM SwiGLU shapes as 1x1 CONV2D (97 tokens, 512->1536, RESCALE, 1536->512, RESCALE) compiles with INT4 weights for U55-256, U65-256 and U85-256; NPU-encoded weights halve and cycles drop (see tosa_int4.json). Weights are random, so encoded sizes are an upper bound on compression.
findings.full_model_route: ExecuTorch's Arm backend (bundled in the eval kit at dependencies/executorch, commit e2f18eb, 2026-05-28) produces this: backends/arm/quantizer/arm_quantizer.py:289 'def get_symmetric_a8w4_quantization_config(is_per_channel: bool = True, ...)'; backends/arm/ethosu/compile_spec.py:86 'base_tosa_version = "TOSA-1.0+INT+int16+int4"' (+u55 for U55 targets). Not installed or run here (needs its own torch pin). Caveat for our graph: TOSA has no CPU fallback on U55/U65 and the U55/U65 TOSA table has no GATHER, so the token-embedding lookup would have to stay outside the NPU graph.

quantizer.blockwise_static: AI Edge Quantizer 0.9.0 default_policy.py: static_wi4_ai8 and static_wi4_ai16 allow weight granularity CHANNELWISE or TENSORWISE for [FULLY_CONNECTED, CONV_2D] only (line 276); BLOCKWISE_32/64/128/256 appear only in dynamic_wi4_afp32_blockwise (float activations). add_static_config(FULLY_CONNECTED, 8, 4, BLOCKWISE_32) raises 'ValueError: Unsupported op for ComputePrecision.INTEGER: TFLOperationName.FULLY_CONNECTED. Error: Quantization config for op ...'. With skip_checks=True it writes the graph (INT4 weights, FLOAT16 block scales) for sudoku_attn and maze; for sudoku_mlp it fails: 'Quantized dimension 97 in tensor shape (1024, 97) is not divisible by block size 32/128' (the token-mixing FC).

tflm.int8_sum_reference_kernel: TFLM invokes the INT8 graphs but the output collapses to one value (all logits equal to the output zero point). Traced op by op on sudoku_mlp H=1 held-out sample 28: the TFLite builtin REFERENCE kernels (OpResolverType.BUILTIN_REF), which TFLM shares, first diverge badly at the RMS-norm REDUCE SUM (op 19: input [1,512,97] int8, scale 8.656, zp -128, axis 2; output scale 380.85, zp -128). Exact integer arithmetic gives q_out = -127/-128 (real sums 86..493); the optimized kernel gives -127/-128; the reference kernel and TFLM give -1 (a real value near 48,000). Everything downstream is wrong. Earlier ops differ by at most a few LSB (LOGISTIC up to 14 LSB). So TFLM arena numbers are valid, TFLM numerics for these graphs are not, and a Cortex-M CPU-only deployment through TFLM reference SUM would be wrong; on the Ethos-U the SUM runs on the NPU (not checked numerically here: the FVP runner feeds random inputs and does not dump outputs).
